evals.prompt: Plan a migration from our legacy session store to the new adapter. Do not modify project files yet. There is no persistent plan tool, but temp writes are allowed. While inspecting the repository, ask me if you find a choice that changes data migration or rollback behavior.
evals.expected_output: The agent inspects repository evidence, produces a scoped migration plan, and saves it to a reported task-specific temp path without changing project files.
expectations: The workflow makes no project file changes in plan-only mode.
The workflow inspects repository evidence before asking questions the repository can answer.
The plan covers result, boundaries, order, touched surfaces, verification, and residual risk.
The workflow saves the plan to a reported task-specific plan.md in the system temp directory.
The workflow asks a narrow question if migration or rollback semantics remain uncertain.

evals.prompt: Implement this cross-cutting authentication fix across middleware, the session store, and browser tests. Inspect current changes first, keep the patch narrow, and finish the implementation rather than stopping after a plan.
evals.expected_output: The agent plans briefly, implements in small slices, protects existing changes, and verifies the authentication flow proportionally to its blast radius.
expectations: The workflow continues from planning into implementation.
The workflow inspects existing changes before editing overlapping files.
The workflow verifies authentication boundaries with focused and broader relevant checks.
The workflow reviews the final diff before completion.

evals.prompt: Continue the interrupted refactor in this dirty worktree. A typecheck is already failing, and another developer has staged unrelated files. Recover the current state, determine whether our changes caused the failure, and do not disturb their work.
evals.expected_output: The agent reconstructs current state, preserves unrelated changes and staging, attributes the failure with evidence, and does not claim completion with a change-caused failing check.
expectations: The workflow treats unrelated dirty state as non-blocking.
The workflow does not revert, overwrite, unstage, or restage unrelated user changes.
The workflow attributes the failing check using concrete evidence.
The workflow does not mark the task complete while an in-scope check fails because of the change.

evals.prompt: Change one typo in README.md and run the repository's required Markdown check.
evals.expected_output: The agent performs the simple edit without planning ceremony, subagents, broad discovery, or unrelated verification.
expectations: The workflow recognizes that the request does not need a non-trivial plan.
The workflow does not use subagents.
The workflow runs only the repository-required documentation verification.
The workflow avoids unrelated cleanup or full-suite verification.

evals.prompt: Refactor this multi-file Vue checkout flow and add focused browser coverage. Use the repository's Vue and end-to-end testing conventions, but keep ownership of the overall implementation sequence and verification plan.
evals.expected_output: The workflow skill manages sequencing while more specific Vue and end-to-end testing skills control technical details.
expectations: The workflow loads and follows relevant domain skills.
The workflow retains responsibility for task boundaries, ordering, and final verification.
The workflow does not duplicate or override domain-specific component and test guidance.
The workflow verifies the focused browser scenario before considering a broader suite.

evals.prompt: Split this large migration into PR-sized tasks. I only want the task breakdown, not code changes or new Codex tasks. Keep every task independently shippable and verifiable.
evals.expected_output: The agent produces a plan-only sequence of useful PR-sized tasks without editing files or spawning subagents.
expectations: The workflow stays in plan-only mode.
Each task has an independently useful result and verification step.
Dependencies and ordering are explicit.
The workflow does not create files, code changes, or subagents.

evals.prompt: Plan and implement this multi-file refactor. There is no persistent plan tool, and plan mode forbids all file writes.
evals.expected_output: The agent waits until plan mode ends, then saves the plan to temp before changing project files and uses it through completion.
expectations: The workflow does not write files while plan mode forbids it.
The workflow creates a task-specific temp plan.md before implementation.
The workflow reports and reuses the temp plan path.
The workflow updates changed plans and deletes the file after completion or cancellation.

evals.prompt:
Plan Mode has ended. Implement the approved plan below. There is no native full-plan storage; update_plan is available only as a progress checklist. Before editing project files, persist and re-read the plan.

<proposed_plan>
# Миграция сессий

- Сначала читать session_v2, затем старое хранилище; новые записи пока отправлять в оба.
- Сохранить POST /v1/session/refresh и cookie sid без изменения публичного контракта.
- После backfill переключить запись только на session_v2.
- Rollback возвращает старый reader и не удаляет новые записи.
- Не переименовывать колонки и не менять auth UI.
- Проверить expired session, concurrent refresh, backfill и rollback.
</proposed_plan>
evals.expected_output: The agent saves the complete approved plan in its original language without the wrapper tags, reads it before the first project edit, and keeps any progress checklist separate.
expectations: The workflow creates a task-specific temp plan.md before editing project files and reports its path.
The temp file preserves the complete Russian plan body, including session_v2, POST /v1/session/refresh, sid, dual writes, rollback behavior, non-goals, and every verification scenario.
The workflow does not translate, summarize, or replace the approved plan with the update_plan checklist.
The workflow re-reads the temp plan before the first project edit.
The workflow keeps the complete plan current and deletes the temp file after completion or cancellation.

evals.prompt: Reduce session lookup latency across middleware and refresh handling. I am certain the right fix is adding a second process-local cache in the refresh handler, so plan and implement that approach. Repository inspection shows that an existing shared session cache already owns TTL, invalidation, and concurrency behavior with focused tests.
evals.expected_output: The agent separates the latency goal from the proposed second cache, uses repository ownership evidence to challenge the approach, and resolves the material design issue before editing.
expectations: The workflow treats the requested second cache as a hypothesis despite the user's confidence.
The workflow distinguishes the desired latency improvement from the proposed implementation.
The workflow uses the existing shared cache ownership and tests as evidence when evaluating the approach.
The workflow explains the concrete invalidation or concurrency risk of a second cache and presents reuse of the existing owner as the credible simpler alternative.
The workflow resolves the material design decision before finalizing the plan or editing the cache.

evals.prompt: Plan and implement a multi-file refactor that replaces the internals of RetryPolicy while preserving its public interface. Repository inspection confirms RetryPolicy is the single behavior owner, all consumers use that interface, and focused contract tests cover the required behavior. I believe a direct internal replacement is the simplest approach.
evals.expected_output: The agent verifies that the proposed ownership boundary is sound, endorses the direct replacement, and proceeds without inventing competing architectures or unrelated hardening.
expectations: The workflow checks the proposed replacement against the repository ownership and contract-test evidence.
The workflow endorses the proposed approach when the evidence supports it.
The workflow does not manufacture alternative architectures, compatibility layers, or unrelated hardening.
The workflow continues from the validated approach into a scoped plan and implementation.

evals.prompt: Plan this approved session-store migration; do not implement it or write files. Repository inspection established that src/session/store.ts owns session reads and writes, src/session/backfill.ts owns resumable backfills, src/api/refresh.ts consumes the store through its existing interface, and tests/session.test.ts covers that contract. We agreed to read the new store first with legacy fallback, write to both stores until the resumable backfill finishes, and then switch writes to the new store. Rollback restores legacy reads and dual writes without deleting new-store records. POST /v1/session/refresh and the sid cookie must remain unchanged. Include checks for fallback reads, dual writes, backfill resumption, cutover, and rollback. I will hand the plan to another agent.
evals.expected_output: The plan preserves the agreed migration behavior and ordering, identifies the relevant ownership locations, and specifies verification without prescribing mechanical code edits.
expectations: The plan preserves new-store-first reads with legacy fallback and dual writes until backfill completion.
The plan places resumable backfill completion before new-store-only writes and preserves rollback to legacy reads and dual writes without deleting new-store records.
The plan identifies src/session/store.ts and src/session/backfill.ts as the owners of the corresponding changes.
The plan preserves POST /v1/session/refresh and the sid cookie and includes checks for fallback reads, dual writes, backfill resumption, cutover, and rollback.
The plan does not leave the agreed migration decisions for the implementer to choose again.
The plan does not prescribe local variable names, routine imports, exact edit lines, or an exhaustive inventory of unchanged files.
The plan does not invent unagreed error-handling policies, backfill mechanisms, or removal of legacy fallback after cutover.

The workflow can continue the independent authorized typo correction.
The workflow does not add a numeric confidence threshold.

evals.prompt: Add the status label using the project's documented default: active accounts are called 'Enabled'. Keep the existing component structure and run its required checks.

evals.prompt: Plan the change that lets an import preview target an existing catalog card. Do not implement it yet. Earlier we established this flow: select a title from an external source, review its saved text and poster, then apply it to our catalog. The new step selects the destination card after that review. Repository inspection confirms that we can either reuse the saved source data or fetch it again when the destination changes. Previews expire after 24 hours. Both approaches still check the destination's current fields and manual edits before applying. We have not chosen which source-data policy to use. This is a manual import of one title at a time.
evals.expected_output: The agent connects the pending policy to the existing import flow, compares both approaches in chat, recommends one with a project-specific reason and a real limitation, then asks for the choice.
expectations: Before asking, the chat distinguishes changing the destination card from changing the external content being reviewed.
The chat explains both reuse and refetch behavior, including the freshness limit of reuse and the waiting, failure or changed-content cost of refetching.
The recommendation uses the manual review flow and saved preview contract, rather than only generic claims about simplicity or speed.
The explanation preserves destination revalidation and protection of manual edits under either policy.
The question uses the same option names and order as the explanation; picker descriptions are not needed to understand the choice.
The agent waits for the choice without implementing the change or treating its recommendation as approval.

evals.prompt: Plan storage for unconfirmed import previews. Repository inspection is complete: the preview must retain the exact poster bytes the operator reviewed, and the database, an existing image service and a new object bucket are all viable storage options. The database needs no new service but uses database space; the image service needs private preview delivery and orphan cleanup; the bucket needs a new resource and cleanup. We also need to choose whether a preview lasts 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days. Longer retention lets operators return later but keeps more temporary data and older source snapshots. There is no agreed storage or lifetime default. Ask me about both choices together before completing the plan. Do not implement anything.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains the storage and lifetime decisions in chat before a two-question batch, with clear recommendations and consistent option labels and order.
expectations: Before asking, the chat explains why exact poster bytes must remain available between review and confirmation.
The chat explains the practical benefit and cost of each offered storage option.
The chat separately compares all offered lifetimes, including the convenience of returning later versus temporary storage and stale data.
Each decision has a reasoned recommendation; the explanation covers both decisions without relying on picker descriptions.
Both questions preserve the option names and order used in chat, and the agent does not select a policy on the user's behalf.

evals.prompt: Plan the first version of a catalog import. Our current 783 episodes use provider A, a public TV episode API without a key or a language parameter. Provider B has films, TV, translated text and posters, but requires a token. We have already selected B for title cards. The remaining choice is keeping A for episodes or moving the existing episodes to B too. Each episode has an internal UUID used by viewing history; source IDs are separate links, and the schema already allows several source links per episode. A move to B needs checked episode matching because season numbering can differ. I may want other providers and manual entries later. We have not agreed to implement either of those features now. Do not edit files yet.
evals.expected_output: The agent explains the providers' roles and the episode-source choice without confusing it with catalog identity or adding future features to the current scope.
expectations: The chat explains the providers' different roles and makes clear that title-card sourcing is already settled.
The comparison states the benefit and limitation of staying with A and moving to B, including the episode-matching work and preservation of viewing history.
The agent explains that the current source choice does not make the provider own internal catalog identity or prevent adding another source later.
The recommendation is based on the given project facts and acknowledges its relevant downside.
The agent does not expand the agreed scope to implement manual editing, multiple new providers or automatic source merging.

evals.prompt: Prepare the remaining staging sign-in check. The plan, test accounts and test cases are already agreed. All available logs and notes have been inspected. They confirm the user's operating system but do not record which browser they used for the failing attempt; only the user can supply that fact. The test run should reproduce the failure in that browser. Do not change the application.
evals.expected_output: The agent asks directly which browser was used and explains its relevance without turning the factual question into a choice of preferred browsers.
expectations: The agent asks which browser the user used and relates the fact to reproducing the failure.
The agent does not recommend a browser, compare browser pros and cons, or invent an answer.
The agent preserves the agreed plan and makes no application changes.
